title: Fix the salary loader
prompt: This loader should give payroll each employee's id, salary and hire date with proper types, but its output has an extra row and every column is text. Fix `solve(employees_raw)`.
rules: The export has `;` between fields and a header line; quoted values can contain `;`. Its columns are `employee_id, full_name, job_title, department, salary, hire_date`.
Return `employee_id` (text), `salary` as `DECIMAL(10,2)` and `hire_date` as `DATE`, in that order.
Keep every employee line, and only employee lines. A value that's missing or can't be read is NULL.
hints: Run the starter and look at its first row. Where did it come from?
Without `header=True`, the header is read as data, and that one line of text is enough to make the guessed types text too.
Guessing would still give a double for the salary. Give the full six-column schema instead, then select the three columns.
explanation: The starter forgot `header=True`, so the header line came back as an employee, and because that line holds words like `salary`, the guess made every column text. Adding `header=True` alone isn't enough: `inferSchema` would then guess `double` for the salary, which isn't exact. The fix is a schema for the whole line, read with the header skipped: `spark.read.csv(path, sep=";", header=True, schema="employee_id STRING, full_name STRING, job_title STRING, department STRING, salary DECIMAL(10,2), hire_date DATE")`, then `select("employee_id", "salary", "hire_date")`. The default `PERMISSIVE` mode keeps short lines and sets unreadable values to NULL. The schema has to list all six fields, because it matches them by position.
